On one machine (Docker Compose)

Source: vignettes/articles/install-local.Rmd
install-local.Rmd

The folder local/ runs the whole system with docker compose, no Kubernetes needed. It is the quickest way to try I-SPI, to test a release, or to develop against real services. The automated end-to-end check uses the same stack; see Automated checks.

The whole system on one machine, for trying I-SPI, testing a release, or developing against real services. It runs the same images as the Kubernetes manifests:

Service Image Reached at
i-spi ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi:1.1.1 http://localhost:3838/
dex dexidp/dex:v2.44.0 http://localhost:5556/dex (sign-in)
i-spi-compute-api ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi-compute-api:1.1.0 http://localhost:8000/docs (optional)
i-spi-compute-worker ghcr.io/immunoplex/i-spi-compute-worker:1.1.0 no port
i-spi-compute-redis redis:7.4 no port
postgres postgres:16, schema from ../db localhost:5433 (optional)

All ports are bound to 127.0.0.1: nothing is reachable from other machines.

Requirements

  • Docker with Compose v2 (Docker Desktop on Windows or macOS, Docker Engine on Linux).
  • About 8 GB of disk for the images; the worker image alone is about 5 GB.
  • 4 CPUs and 8 GB of memory for the worker by default. See “Worker size” below.
  • The worker image is built for amd64. On Apple silicon, Docker runs it under emulation, which is much slower.

Start 

cd local
cp .env.example .env      # then replace every change-me, e.g. with: openssl rand -hex 24
docker compose up -d

The first start downloads the images and loads the schema into the new database. Then open http://localhost:3838/ and sign in with:

  • Email: ispi-user@example.org
  • Password: ispi-local

dex.yaml holds this account; how to change the password is described there.

What to expect on first use

The database starts empty: no projects, studies or data. In I-SPI: 1. Create a project. 2. Create a study. 3. Import plates. 4. Run a fit.

The fit goes to the local worker. Its progress shows in I-SPI, and the results appear in the study’s views and in Data > Results.

Day to day 

docker compose ps                              # what is running
docker compose logs -f i-spi                   # I-SPI log (sign-in, errors)
docker compose logs -f i-spi-compute-worker    # fitting
docker compose stop                            # stop, keep the data
docker compose up -d                           # start again
docker compose down -v                         # remove everything, including the database

To look at the database: psql "host=localhost port=5433 dbname=immunoplex user=postgres sslmode=require", with the password from .env.

Worker size

WORKER_CORES, WORKER_CPUS and WORKER_MEMORY in .env size the worker: - WORKER_CORES caps how many curves it fits in parallel and its Stan chains. It must not exceed WORKER_CPUS. - The worker plans its parallel fits against WORKER_MEMORY.

Bayesian fits of large studies want more of both; production runs with 16 CPUs and 16 GB.

Upgrading

Change the image tags in docker-compose.yml and run docker compose up -d. The database keeps its data. If a new i-spi-compute release brings a new calib schema version, apply that release’s migration from i-spi-compute worker/migrations/ to the existing database before starting the new worker. ../db is only loaded into an empty database.

How it differs from the Kubernetes install

  • No Traefik, TLS or hostname: everything is plain HTTP on localhost.
  • Dex keeps no database: it has one fixed account, and no signup page.
  • PostgreSQL uses the image’s self-signed certificate. I-SPI and the worker always connect with TLS, as in production.
